meanings.note: aller + infinitive: tu vas l'agacer = you're going to annoy her
Je vais déjeuner. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to go'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'allé').
Imperative used to encourage. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to go'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'allé').

examples.trans: I'm going to have lunch twice.

examples.text: Il arrête de travailler à six heures.
Sans toi, je crois que j'arrêterais ce métier.
examples.trans: Without you, I think I'd quit this job.

meanings.note: j'en ai assez = I've had enough, I'm fed up
Assez bien. Invariable French adverb meaning 'enough'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

Il vous attend?. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to wait (for); to expect'.

examples.text: Attendez-moi deux minutes devant le bureau!
examples.trans: Wait two minutes for me in front of the office!

examples.text: Nous attendons un appel très important de Los Angeles.
examples.trans: We are waiting for a very important call from Los Angeles.

meanings.note: à + le contracted: au boulot, au téléphone

examples.trans: I've got a problem at work.

Masculine noun ('le bateau', plural 'les bateaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'boat'.

examples.text: Mais trois mois de tournage, sur un bateau, en pleine mer!
examples.trans: But three months of shooting, on a boat, out at sea!

meanings.note: Une rivière qui coule. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to flow'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'coulé').
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to flow'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'coulé').

examples.text: Une rivière qui coule? Des animaux qui gambadent dans les bois?
examples.trans: A flowing river? Animals frolicking in the woods?

meanings.note: Je ne crois pas = I don't think so. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to believe, to think'.
Je ne crois pas = I don't think so. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to believe, to think'.
D' before a vowel. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
le film de Tarantino = Tarantino's film
Also 'some': du sucre. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
À demain = see you tomorrow. Invariable French adverb meaning 'tomorrow'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.
examples.trans: And tomorrow you're having lunch with Audiard.

meanings.note: Demander quelque chose à quelqu'un. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to ask'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'demandé').

examples.text: Si vous avez besoin d'aide, demandez.
examples.trans: If you need help, just ask.

meanings.note: dire la vérité à quelqu'un = to tell someone the truth
dire à quelqu'un; dis-lui = tell her/him

examples.text: Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir.
Appelle Clémentine. Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
examples.trans: Call Clémentine. Tell her I can't come tonight.

meanings.note: se tenir droit(e) = to stand up straight
À droite = on the right. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'straight'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Emmanuel, elle doit se tenir droite.
examples.trans: Emmanuel, she must stand up straight.

meanings.note: Un verre d'eau = a glass of water. Feminine noun ('la eau', plural 'les eaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'water'.

examples.text: Un verre d'eau, s'il vous plaît.

examples.trans: No, thank you. A glass of water.

meanings.note: for a feminine noun: l'industrie... elle
for a feminine noun: l'industrie... elle

examples.text: Écoute, c'est une industrie, et elle est pleine de requins.
examples.trans: Listen, it's an industry, and it's full of sharks.

meanings.note: j'ai encore un agent? = do I still have an agent?
Invariable French adverb meaning 'still'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.trans: Do I still have an agent here?

meanings.note: Fermer la porte. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to close'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'fermé').
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to close'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'fermé').

examples.text: Maintenez la porte fermée et tirez les rideaux.
examples.trans: Hold the door closed and draw the curtains.

foncer.gloss: to go for it, rush ahead

meanings.en: to rush boldly forward, go for it
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to go for it'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'foncé').

examples.trans: It's a great opportunity, go for it!
You like her very much. Go for it!

examples.text: Maintenant, tu dois foncer au casting.
examples.trans: Now, you must hurry to the casting.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le iceberg', plural 'les icebergs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'iceberg'.

examples.text: Ce problème n'est que la partie visible de l'iceberg.
examples.trans: This problem is only the tip of the iceberg.

examples.text: Le navire essaie d'éviter un immense iceberg.
examples.trans: The ship is trying to avoid a huge iceberg.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'here'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Laissez vos photos et votre CV ici.
examples.trans: Leave your photos and your CV here.

meanings.note: Never changes for plural. Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'there is', common in natural conversation.
il y a trois semaines = three weeks ago

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?
Non, c'est la place de Samuel. Il est mort il y a six jours.
examples.trans: No, it's Samuel's place. He died six days ago.

meanings.note: J' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'I'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: Adverb: je veux juste. Invariable French adverb meaning 'just'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
Adjective. Invariable French adverb meaning 'just'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.trans: I just want to see Mathias.

examples.text: Oui, oui. J'ai juste besoin d'un petit cours.
examples.trans: Yes, yes. I just need a little lesson.

meanings.note: definite article; l' before a vowel

examples.text: C'est le prochain film de Tarantino.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la morgue', plural 'les morgues') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'morgue'.

examples.text: La scène se passe dans une morgue.
examples.trans: The scene takes place in a morgue.

examples.text: Le médecin entre dans la morgue.
Or votre scène se passe à la morgue.
examples.trans: Yet your scene takes place in the morgue.

meanings.note: Informal: maman. Feminine noun ('la mère', plural 'les mères') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'mother'.
ne... pas = not; ne... rien = nothing; ne... que = only; n' before a vowel

examples.text: Tarantino ne prendra pas Cécile. Problème d'âge.

examples.text: Un mouvement de panique a gagné toute l'équipe.
examples.trans: A wave of panic swept through the whole team.

+ infinitive: pour voir. Core French preposition meaning 'for', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Je suis là pour voir Mathias.

examples.trans: It's like a dream for me.

examples.trans: How old would you say she is?

examples.text: À quel âge ces caprices s'arrêtent-ils?
examples.trans: At what age do these whims stop?

meanings.note: Quelqu'un de jeune = someone young. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'someone'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Quelqu'un a dit à Cécile qu'elle était trop vieille pour le rôle.
examples.trans: Someone told Cécile she was too old for the part.

meanings.note: c'est moi qui... = I'm the one who...
Qui parle?. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'who'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.trans: I'm the one who trained you!

examples.text: Tu ne pars pas. C'est moi qui te vire!
examples.trans: You're not leaving. I'm the one firing you!

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to jump'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'sauté').

examples.text: Mais je ne saute pas sur le canard!
examples.trans: But I'm not jumping on the duck!

examples.text: Je ne saute pas sur le canard, c'est clair?
examples.trans: I'm not jumping on the duck, is that clear?

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to save'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'sauvé').

examples.text: J'ai sauvé une cliente de l'agence, c'est tout.
examples.trans: I saved one of the agency's clients, that's all.

savoir.gloss: to know; to know how to

meanings.note: Je ne sais pas = I don't know. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to know; to know how to'.
+ infinitive: savoir monter. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to know; to know how to'.

examples.trans: Do you know where he is?

meanings.note: part of verbs like se passer, s'occuper; s' before a vowel

examples.text: Ça ne se passe pas bien?

meanings.note: Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'solution, answer'.

examples.text: Une solution? Une grande actrice de quatre-vingts ans, libre dans trois semaines?
examples.trans: A solution? A great eighty-year-old actress, free in three weeks?

meanings.note: Sous la pluie = in the rain. Core French preposition meaning 'under', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Sous la pluie? Bréhier va m'entendre!
examples.trans: In the rain? Bréhier will hear from me!

examples.text: Le chat dort sous la table.
examples.trans: The cat sleeps under the table.

examples.text: Un rôle de professeur sous la pluie.
examples.trans: A role of teacher in the rain.

meanings.note: Sur la table, sur la route. Core French preposition meaning 'on', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Sur haut-parleur = on speaker. Core French preposition meaning 'on', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Le livre est sur la table.
examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: Attention, tu arrives sur la route!
examples.trans: Careful, you're heading for the road!

meanings.note: Avoir du talent = to be talented. Masculine noun ('le talent', plural 'les talents') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'talent'.

examples.text: Oui, Quentin a beaucoup de talent.
examples.trans: Yes, Quentin has a lot of talent.

meanings.note: takes a singular verb: tout le monde est là

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.note: Aller au tribunal = to go to court. Masculine noun ('le tribunal', plural 'les tribunaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'court'.

examples.text: Si tu pars avec tes acteurs, on va au tribunal!
examples.trans: If you leave with your actors, we're going to court!

meanings.note: trésorerie disponible = available cash reserves

examples.text: Je n'ai plus aucune trésorerie disponible.
examples.trans: I have no cash reserves left.
